wants_socket and hold_socket each check wantDisk/usedDisk under the same controller mutex. usedDisk is set only after capturing the real successful completed write job continuation and immediately before DiskHeld is appended in that critical section. The original receive body runs unmodified until that real disk hold is established. This avoids holding a partial receive before the first disk job can exist; it invents no job or received bytes.

When disk hold is not requested, the new condition is vacuous; disk-only never admits a socket as before. Existing allowHolds/target/usedSocket checks remain. release_all_and_wait atomically disarms future admissions, queues both real releases before waiting, invokes captured code outside the controller mutex and precedes all Worker owner/thread joins. The ordering amendment adds no wait, timer, thread, alert consumer or production owner change.

usedDisk means an actual disk hold occurred, not a general promise of continued occupancy after arbitrary caller release. The combined test releases neither gate before its occupied snapshot and independently requires simultaneous diskHeld/socketHeld/live owner; positive byte counts, exactly one hold each, DiskHeld<SocketHeld and no prior release event establish the intended stronger test precondition.

All original case names, assertions, wait deadlines and payload/receipt checks remain, with only the explicit test-only image identity moving v1 to v2. Both earlier single-hold proof bodies are byte-exact under the first amendment. Final trace adds only a helper and one declaration in each of the three existing methods. Planned test row count remains five; no actual v2 result is claimed.

All three local declarations are ordered fixture, Gates, TraceOnExit, Worker. Reverse destruction therefore releases/disarms callbacks and closes/joins the Worker, then snapshots/prints diagnostics, then finishes the controller, then destroys the fixture. Constructor failure before Worker completion still leaves Gates cleanup. Worker source and its exceptional owner/lease lifetime protection are byte-identical to original 83ec.

snapshot copies the fixed-capacity scalar ledger while holding the controller mutex and releases that mutex before qInfo formatting. TraceOnExit holds only a static literal name, adds no owner/callback/packet reference, consumes no alerts and emits no causal certification event. Qt logging may allocate or fail catastrophically; this occurs after successful Worker release/join and is not promised to be allocation-failure-safe or to survive SIGKILL/terminate. A missing diagnostic cannot count as causal PASS.

The partial-payload scheduling diagnosis remains labelled inference: the occupied combined-case ledger did not exist before its v1 wait failure. The retained v1 image/build record and raw failures are unchanged. Individual existing successful v1 proofs do not certify the new simultaneous schedule; a fresh v2 source-bound image/catalog and actual traces are still required.
